deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page to reconstruct. It carries no text, formula or numeral. Near the upper left there is a single small pen sketch: two small circles of roughly equal size, joined by a short horizontal line between them. From the bottom of each circle a long, roughly vertical line runs downward. The right-hand line is slightly longer and appears to be drawn twice, or retraced. The rest of the leaf is blank, apart from paper stains and a small tear at the top right.

The drawing is not labelled, so its purpose is a matter of interpretation. Possible readings, none of them certain:
(a) Two conducting spheres on vertical stands or stems, joined by a wire. This is the standard setup for charge sharing between connected conductors, and it would fit Riemann's interest in electrostatics and electrodynamics and the mention of 'Weber' and 'Auditorium' on the next page.
(b) Two bodies at the ends of vertical lines, coupled by a horizontal link. This would be a schematic coupled pendulum, though drawn inverted, since the circles sit on top.
(c) An idle doodle, perhaps a pair of spectacles or pins.

I do not add any derivation, because nothing on the page supports one. The next page is a letter draft dated 24 September 1858. It contains another schematic sketch and the relation dx/dq = x, but that cannot be securely tied to this drawing.

results.what: Unlabelled schematic sketch: two circles joined by a horizontal line, each with a vertical line descending from it. Possibly two conductors on stands joined by a wire, or a coupled-pendulum schematic.
results.modern_name: None (no mathematical content); at most a schematic of a physical apparatus
